'''Lauri Markkanen''' (born May 22, 1997) is a Finnish [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona]]. He is the son of Finnish basketball players [[Pekka Markkanen|Pekka]] and Riikka Markkanen.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.wildcat.arizona.edu/article/2016/11/household-rivalry-lauri-markkanen-poised-to-emerge-as-best-in-family|title=Household rivalry: Lauri Markkanen poised to emerge as best in family|work=The Daily Wildcat|access-date=2017-05-12}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Markkanen grew up in [[Jyväskylä]], and played his junior years in local team HoNsU.<ref>{{cite news|title= Koripallon poikkeuslahjakkuus Lauri Markkanen harjoitteli heittoja jopa ilman pakkasrajaa|url=http://www.hs.fi/urheilu/art-2000002889803.html|work=Helsingin Sanomat|date=6 March 2016|language=fi-FI}}</ref> Markkanen played for HBA-Märsky in Finland from 2014 to 2016.

==College career==

===Arizona (2016–2017)===

===Freshman season===
On October 17, 2015, Markkanen verbally committed to NCAA Division I squad [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] Wildcats prior to the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=UA basketball: Finnish big man Markkanen commits|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|date=October 17, 2015|url=http://tucson.com/sports/basketball/college/wildcats/ua-basketball-finnish-big-man-markkanen-commits/article_e966bcd3-c48f-5d2d-9ff6-14c271e92a71.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Finnish forward Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|publisher=Sports Illustrated|author=Jeremy Woo|date=October 17, 2015|url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/10/17/arizona-wildcats-lauri-markkanen-commits-finland-sean-miller}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Finland's five-star forward Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|author=Sam Vecenie|publisher=CBS Sports|date=October 17, 2015|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25343238/finlands-five-star-forward-lauri-markkanen-commits-to-arizona}}</ref> Lauri signed a letter to intent to Arizona on Nov. 11th. ESPN.com reported that the seven-foot Finn is considered "a possible one-and-done candidate for the NBA draft."<ref name="ESPN">{{cite news|title=Finnish big man Lauri Markkanen commits to Arizona|publisher=ESPN.com|date=|author=Jeff Borzello|url=http://espn.go.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13908331/finnish-center-lauri-markkanen-commits-arizona-wildcats}}</ref> He became the first player since [[Mike Bibby]] to wear the jersey number 10. He recorded a career high 30 points, 12 field goals made & 18 shot attempts on Jan. 12th against rival [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]]. Also recording a career high 13 rebounds 3 times against [[Northern Colorado Bears men's basketball|Northern Colorad]]<nowiki/>o(11/21/17), [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]](1/26/17) & [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] (2/18/17). His career high 3 blocks came against ASU in the regular season finale Mar. 4th, 2017.

Markkanen was selected to the third team All-American team in AP, NBC Sports, USA Today and Sporting News on March 6, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/college-basketball-all-americans-2017-sporting-news-lonzo-ball-josh-hart-justin-jackson-frank-mason-caleb-swanigan/1tnhntha9fb3q1b468aho78tbp|title=2017 All Americans|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=}}</ref> He was a first team all Pac-12 selection, as well as first team all Pac-12 Freshman team and first team all Pac-12 team in Associated Press.

At the conclusion of his freshman season, Markkanen announced his intention to forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA Draft]] where he is projected as a first round selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizona-wildcats-freshman-lauri-markkanen-confirms-he-ll-leave-for/article_3db2a624-156a-11e7-931e-83d630618d4c.html|title=Arizona Wildcats freshman Lauri Markkanen confirms he'll leave for NBA |website=tucson.com|author=Bruce Pascoe|date=2017-03-30|accessdate=2017-03-30}}</ref>

==National team career==
Markkanen made his international debut with the Finnish U-18 national team at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article102553812.html|title=Former KU forward Pekka Markkanen’s son, Lauri, expected to excel at Arizona|work=kansascity|access-date=2017-05-12|language=en}}</ref> Markkanen averaged 18.2 points per game to lead the FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship in the summer of 2015.<ref name=ESPN/> He was the top scorer in [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] tournament with average of 24.9 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=All-Star Five - Lauri Markkanen is the top scorer! - FIBA U20 European Championship 2016 - FIBA U20 European Championship Division A 2016 - FIBA.com|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u20/2016/videos/All-Star-Five-Lauri-Markkanen-is-the-top-scorer|website=FIBA.com|accessdate=24 January 2017|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son of [[Pekka Markkanen|Pekka]] (who played NCAA basketball at Kansas)<ref name=ESPN/> and Riikka Markkanen, and has two brothers, Miikka and professional soccer player, [[Eero Markkanen]].

Markkanen's father, Pekka in his career reached the level of the Finnish national basketball team, and his mother Riikka (née Ellonen) reached the basketball championship silver, and also appeared in the national team level.
